children: The $4.3 bln toy maker behind Barbie is under pressure from activists. A mooted $6 bln bid from Authentic Brands would fill the void caused by a leadership transition. New boss Roger Lynch might be able to turn the ship, but persuading investors to play along is next level.
Full view will be published shortly.

Investment firm Ariel Investments, a major shareholder in Mattel, urged the Barbie maker on October 5 to explore a sale as its performance and profitability has stalled, according to a letter seen by Reuters. Shares of Mattel rose roughly 19% on October 2 after The Wall Street Journal reported the company had attracted takeover interest from Authentic Brands Group at more than $20 per share.

Mattel named on September 30 Roger Lynch as its new chairman and chief executive replacing Ynon Kreiz. Lynch was director at Mattel and previously served as CEO of publisher Conde Nast. Kreiz was named co-chief executive of Paramount Skydance on the same day.
